## 1. THE MASTER ARC REPORT

**PUBLIC PRICING — PRESENT, but as a CATEGORY pricing, not a person pricing. This is the single most important finding in the file.**

The world never measures Alaina and finds her wanting. It excludes her *before* measurement, on a law about what she is. The instrument is **Commonwealth inheritance law** and it prices her at zero the moment she is born a girl — and the law is stated **only in narration** (Ep 2: *"only male family members could inherit"*; Ep 3: *"Not a single woman, no matter how much she trained… could withstand that kind of recoil"*). **No character says it aloud in twenty episodes.**

What IS spoken is the pricing by proxy — the branch family arriving to take the dead man's legacy, with courtesy:
- *"We must ensure that Major General Caius Valerius's sacrifice was not in vain. We are not denying Young Lord Alain Valerius's right to his inheritance. We are simply asking that the Valerius family choose its most outstanding child…"* (Soren, Ep 6)
- *"The Valerius family made Caius. … We can certainly make another."* (Soren, Ep 7)
- *"Lady Valerius, it's not too late. Retract your wager, and the Valerius family will raise Alaina with the utmost care."* (Soren, Ep 8 — she is priced as a dependent, not a candidate)
- The rival child's readout: *"Physical Fitness S Rank, Spiritual Power Tier One, and Potential A Plus Rank … Excellent. Recommended for accelerated development."* (Ep 8)

**RE-PRICING — PRESENT and clean, at the same instrument, minutes later.** The military's own top-of-the-line assessment device, brought in at Soren's request:

> *"Physical Fitness: S Rank / Spiritual Power: Tier Two / Potential: S Rank / Assessment Overview: Exceptional. Recommended for maximum priority development."* (Ep 8 — four separate lines in source)

Capped by *"Soren, … You know the way out."* (Seraphina) and the enemy's exit grunt *"Hmph. Let's go!"*

A **second, private re-pricing** fires at Ep 18 on a different instrument — the tempering bath: *"The results were far better than we ever could have hoped. Her metrics improved by thirty to eighty percent across the board."* (Elara) → *"Really?!"* → *"God bless the Valerius family."* (Quentin, twice). The benchmark that makes the number land — Caius's all-time family record of 10–50% — is **narration and must be voiced**.

**Authorship note for W3 — three hard gaps.**

1. **No witness ever speaks at a re-pricing.** All three recognition beats in eps 1–20 — the newborn pod alarm (Ep 3), the assessment reversal (Ep 8), the ten-vial absorption (Ep 10) — are delivered by a machine readout or by narration, with **zero spoken reaction from the room**. For an audio-first promo, the reaction lines do not exist and must be authored.
2. **The cruellest law is never in a mouth.** Both load-bearing rules (male-only inheritance; no woman can pilot an Imperator) are narration. Putting one in an authority's mouth is the highest-value writing job in the whole source.
3. **The win is a lie and the source knows it.** The re-pricing is won by a girl the room believes is a boy. The victory *deepens* the concealment rather than relieving it — which is the natural resolution-withhold.

**Ruled promo arc: PRICING-BY-CATEGORY → THE WAGER → RE-PRICING → THE TAX.** The wager (eps 7–8) is this source's spine, exactly as it is in RBM. Do not end on the win; end on what the win costs — *"Tell Uncle Quentin, that Young Lord Alain Valerius and I are both fine."*

## 4. HARVEST — EXCHANGE SHAPES

**a) The wager escalation ladder** (Eps 7–8, Seraphina ↔ Soren, two state witnesses) — flag KEEP-VERBATIM.
Reasonable-sounding proposal ("We are simply asking that the Valerius family choose its most outstanding child…") → bloodline counter ("Need I remind you, my husband was an Imperator.") → total counter-stake naming both sides ("If Alain inherits, then every other member of the Valerius family will be exiled from Dominion. Immediately.") → the private whisper that reframes it as desperation ("She could be bluffing.") → public acceptance with a crueller counter-stake ("she will be barred from joining any military system of the Commonwealth") → the instrument runs → the loser dismissed ("You know the way out."). **This is the source's spine and its single most reusable shape.**

**b) The deflection ladder against authority** (Ep 7, Seraphina ↔ military rep ↔ government official) — flag KEEP-VERBATIM.
Appeal to duty ("Surely the military has an opinion on that?") → pleasant institutional non-answer ("The military does not allow the child of a hero to be bullied.") → the second official's silence → contempt spoken flat ("So this is the government. And this is the military. I see now.") → both smiles freeze. *Silence is the third participant.*

**c) Mercy-offer-refused, mirrored** (Ep 8, Soren ↔ Seraphina) — flag KEEP-VERBATIM.
She offers him the exit first ("if you're willing to give up on the inheritance right now, I can be merciful") → refused → he offers her the exit at his high-water mark ("it's not too late. Retract your wager") → refused → measurement → reversal. *The same courtesy runs twice, in both directions, and neither takes it.*

**d) Plea into erasure** (Ep 2, Seraphina → unborn Alaina → the room) — flag KEEP-VERBATIM.
One-sided bargaining with a child who can hear ("Even if you're mad at me for making you live a different kind of life, you have to come out and yell at me for it, right?") → compliance → the birth cry → the immediate public renaming order to staff ("Tell Uncle Quentin, that Young Lord Alain Valerius and I are both fine."). *Intimacy and erasure in one unbroken run — the show's thesis in ninety seconds.*

**e) The withheld-truth interrogation ladder** (Ep 4, reprised comically Ep 10, Alaina ↔ Little Four) — flag KEEP-VERBATIM.
Demand for identity → wary credential recital ("Mecha learning device number four-four-four-four…") → dismissive brag → the suspicion beat ("Is there something you're not telling me?") → confession → the confessor's panic → forgiveness. The Ep-10 reprise runs the identical turns and lands on deadpan ("Did I not tell you? I guess it just slipped my mind."). *The show's house pattern, not a one-off.*

**f) The bait-the-spend wager stack** (Eps 16–17, Number One / system ↔ Alaina) — flag KEEP-VERBATIM.
Payout announced → rules explained with a loaded word → the probe ("Does that mean honor points aren't easy to come by?") → answered with silence → a forced ten-minute clock → the hero underspends ("I only want this one.") → the scoff ("Are you really going to waste them?") → the counter-question ("Will they really be wasted?") → the clock expires → the system pays off. *Trap → probe → silence → deadline → refusal → counter-stake → vindication.*

**g) Punishment menu → all-in wager** (Ep 20, system / Number One ↔ Alaina) — flag KEEP-VERBATIM.
Verdict with a percentage ("mastery of the ninth stance at sixty nine percent. Mission incomplete.") → three-option punishment menu → the command to answer ("Speak. Which do you choose?") → the hero asks terms on option three → terms named with the downside doubled → the choice taken in silence → exit on a threatening glare.

**h) Result-reveal ladder into the wrong explanation** (Ep 18, Quentin ↔ Elara) — flag KEEP-VERBATIM.
Anxious question ("How did it go?") → the number ("thirty to eighty percent across the board") → disbelief ("Really?!") → confirming nod → collapse into awe ("God bless the Valerius family") → **the credit misassigned** ("It seems the Young Lord inherited all of Master Caius's best physical traits"). *Recognition and erasure in the same breath — the show's whole engine in six turns.*

## 5. THE THIN-SLOT REPORT (authorship map)

- **SLOT 1 / SLOT 16 — THE LAW IS NEVER SPOKEN. The single highest-value authorship job in the source.** Both load-bearing rules live only in narration: *"only male family members could inherit"* (Ep 2) and *"Not a single woman, no matter how much she trained or built up her muscle mass, could withstand that kind of recoil"* (Ep 3). W3 must put one of them in an authority's mouth — the government representative and Soren are the two available mouths, and Soren is the better one because he can weaponise it. **Without this line the promo has no stated injustice, only an implied one, and the injustice engine will not fire.**
- **SLOT 21 — THE RECOGNITION DROP: MISSING in eps 1–10, weak overall.** Three collapse-into-deference beats occur and all three are narrated. This is also structurally *correct* for the show — she is hiding, so nobody may recognise her — which makes it the withheld payoff, not a defect. W3 authors the drop as **promise, not event**. The verbatim anchor for what recognition will look like is the machine's own reversal at Ep 8.
- **SLOT 9 — COST-OF-BEING-RIGHT: present in shape, absent in dialogue.** The show's sharpest instance — Elara reading her silence in the venom bath as *"faulty pain receptors"* and resolving to escalate the training until she feels *"real"* pain (Ep 18) — is narration, and the narrator explicitly flags it as the seed of future suffering. **Author this as a spoken line.** It is the cruellest ACT → PUNISHMENT in twenty episodes and it is currently unusable.
- **SLOT 3 — SACRIFICE LINE: partial.** The father's life is covered; the *material* family sacrifice is absent. Nobody says what this cost them.
- **SLOT 7 — DEADPAN ACCEPTANCE: eps 1–10 only.** All five instances are Seraphina or Little Four. Alaina herself never gets one, because she is pre-verbal for most of the band.
- **SLOT 22 — DEATHBED CHARGE: variant only.** Caius dies before she exists and speaks only to his wife. There is no interrupted word and no charge to the hero. The function is real but displaced.
- **IMAGE CLASS H — DESTROYED TOKEN: EMPTY.** Nothing the hero loves is broken in public in twenty episodes. Ask the operator whether to author one; the sealed printout (Ep 3) is the obvious candidate object.
- **No antagonist supply after Ep 8.** Soren exits in Ep 8 and never returns; the Ep-14 noblewoman gets two lines. Eps 11–20 have **no human antagonist at all** — the pressure comes from institutions (the clock, the bath, the martial-arts quota), none of which can be insulted, negotiated with, or made to recognise her. **Any build weighted toward eps 11–20 will be short of an opposing face.**
- **Every triumph is private.** Triple-S rank: one instructor. Record bath metrics: two servants in a corridor while she sleeps. The Ep-20 mastery: nobody. **There is no room to go silent anywhere in eps 11–20.** The only public room in the entire source is the Ep 7–8 inheritance hall — build there.
- **Structural ruling:** run the master arc **PRICING-BY-CATEGORY → THE WAGER → RE-PRICING → THE TAX**, which the source supports verbatim end to end within eps 1–8. Do not end on the win; end on the cost of it.

## 6. FREE HARVEST (≤10)

1. **"Mecha learning device number four-four-four-four-four-four-four-four-four, from the Mechanical Kingdom of the Mandora star system. And also, your contracted long-term companion."** (Little Four, Ep 4) — nine spelled-out "four"s. An audio gift; reproduce exactly.
2. **"It's flat. " … "Thank God, I'm still a girl."** (Alaina, Ep 5) — the entire premise landing in a newborn's private relief, seconds after her mother renames her. The best cold-open button in the source.
3. **"Darling, stop torturing Mommy. Come out and meet me, please. Even if you're mad at me for making you live a different kind of life, you have to come out and yell at me for it, right?"** (Seraphina, Ep 2) — an apology, permission to be hated, and love, delivered pre-birth. The hardest line in the corpus.
4. **"Whoo, good thing I'm quick! Otherwise, they would've found out my host's secret. When I meet her later, she'd better praise me big time for this, hehe!"** (Little Four, Ep 3) — the save happens *inside* the pod alarm; the audience knows before the room does.
5. **"I taste something delicious! I know this taste! No, wait something's wrong. Ugh, what is this garbage? It's full of junk! It completely ruins the flavor!"** (Little Four, Ep 9) — a serum worth more than cities, reviewed as a cheap knockoff, mid-injection.
6. **"Bring this Young Lord an extra large steak!"** (Alaina, Ep 18) — the disguise spoken aloud by a four-year-old who has just resolved to diet.
7. **"Hey, don't think you can bribe me just by being nice! I, Little Four, am a being of high moral character! I'll never compromise my principles, no matter what."** (Little Four, Ep 11) — the companion's whole engine in one breath.
8. **"Whoever controls the information, controls everything."** (Little Four, Ep 15) — the AI's stated rationale for wanting the net; sits oddly and brilliantly in a toddler's mouth.
9. **"And the other four percent. Why does it feel so familiar? Is it poison? Yep, looks like some kind of snake venom. And what's this? Scorpion? A centipede, and spider venom!"** (Little Four, Ep 17) — the family's secret formula priced in horrors, as an escalating list.
10. **"Back in the hovercar, when Valerius  Seven spoke, I thought I'd finally found one of my own kind in this world. I was so happy. I've never met anyone like me since leaving Mandora. It's been lonely."** (Little Four, Ep 15) — the loneliness confession that upgrades the bond from contract to family. *(Source has a double space in "Valerius  Seven.")*
